summary: Server crashes when critical arrow with very high damage value hits an entity
description: The bug When an arrow with a very high damage value (or a really high speed) deals critical damage and hits an entity, the server can crash. [ (20w17a) crash-2020-04-28_22.27.03-server.txt] Description: Ticking entity java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: bound must be positive at java.util.Random.nextInt(Random.java:388) at bdb.a(SourceFile:351) at bdn.a(SourceFile:118) at bdb.h(SourceFile:227) at bdd.h(SourceFile:103) at yr.a(SourceFile:584) at yr Lambda 3446 120053388.accept(Unknown Source) at boq.a(SourceFile:577) at yr.a(SourceFile:399) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.b(SourceFile:827) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.a(SourceFile:766) at enn.a(SourceFile:89) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.run(SourceFile:625) at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:745) Reproduction steps - Switch to Survival mode - execute at s anchored eyes run summon arrow 3 {damage:1e100d,crit:1b} The game crashes once the arrow hits you Code analysis 20w17a, Mojang names The fix for MC-87655 made sure, that the damage value used for damage calculation is always 0. However, if the result of damage speed becomes Integer.MAX_VALUE the result overflows and becomes negative (see MC-181312). If the arrow is dealing critical damage (crit:1b), this negative value is passed to java.util.Random.nextInt(int), the exception seen in the crash report is thrown. If only MC-181312 was fixed, the calculated damage would overflow after adding the critical damage bonus, which might currently not cause any crashes, but could in the future. Therefore, it would make sense to clamp the damage to a maximum (e.g. of Integer.MAX_VALUE 2, or even smaller) since higher damage will likely never occur in vanilla gameplay anyway and would likely kill any entity instantaneously.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition.
2. Switch to Survival mode.
3. Execute the command: `execute at s anchored eyes run summon arrow 3 {damage:1e100d,crit:1b}`.
4. Wait for the arrow to hit you.
5. Observe that the server crashes upon impact.
Observed Behavior: When an arrow with an extremely high damage value or high speed strikes an entity and deals critical damage, the server experiences a crash. The crash report indicates a ticking entity error, specifically a java.lang.IllegalArgumentException stating that the bound must be positive. This occurs because the damage calculation process, which should ensure the damage value is zero, instead results in an overflow when the damage speed reaches Integer.MAX_VALUE, turning the value negative. This negative value is subsequently passed to the java.util.Random.nextInt method, leading to the exception that causes the server crash. To reproduce this bug, players can switch to Survival mode and execute a command to summon an arrow with a damage value of 1e100d and critical hit enabled. Upon impact, the server crashes. The underlying issue stems from a previous fix that did not account for critical damage bonuses, which could cause the damage to overflow and potentially lead to future crashes. To prevent this, it is advisable to clamp the damage to a maximum value, such as Integer.MAX_VALUE or a smaller threshold, since damage values exceeding this are unlikely to occur in standard gameplay and could result in instant kills to any entity.
Expected Behavior: When the arrow with a very high damage value hits an entity, the server should process the damage calculation without crashing. Instead of encountering an exception due to an overflow, the game should correctly apply the damage value, ensuring that it remains within a safe range. The entity should take the appropriate amount of damage, and the server should continue running smoothly, allowing for normal gameplay without interruptions.
